newsitem.title: USA: Lernout & Hauspie to buy Kurzweil.
newsitem.headline: Lernout & Hauspie to buy Kurzweil.

text.p: Lernout & Hauspie Speech Products said on Tuesday it signed a definitive agreement to buy Kurzweil Applied Intelligence Inc for about $53 million.

Both companies develop technologies and products which allow personal computers and other devices to recognize spoken words and convert them into text or automatically perform operations, Lernout said.
As a result of the acquisition, Lernout & Hauspie said it would work with Kurzweil to develop a large vocabulary, speaker-independent, continuous dictation engine.
The company said it believed the joint effort would help accelerate its introduction of continuous speech dictation products by about six months.

Lernout said 80 percent of the purchase price would be paid in cash and 20 percent would be paid in newly-issued Lernout shares. It said it believed it had or could obtain enough financial reserves to cover the acquisition.
The purchase, set to be completed within a few months, was expected to be non-dilutive to earnings per share in 1997 and accretive in 1998, the company said.

Lernout also said it was in talks with the Dictation Consortium, a Flanders Language Valley Foundation investment dedicated to automatic speech recognition, for the consortium to participate in the acquisition.
Under proposed terms, the consortium would pay Lernout up to $26 million out of income seen from 1998 products, it said.
The company also said the acquisition would boost revenues from its continuous dictation products.

Kurzeil President Tom Brew said: "Kurzweil AI is in the final stage of an extensive business transition. Both our medical software and PC applications groups are benefiting from new products that were introduced during the past 12 months." Brew was expected to leave to pursue other business opportunities when the deal was completed but would remain a consultant to the company, Lernout said.
Kurzweil is based in Waltham, Mass.
